segments.headline: Can AI models run real robots?

beats.narration: This robot learned to move only in simulation. Can it work for real?

beats.narration: Frontier AI models, like GPT-6 Astra, can now control robots directly.

beats.narration: In SenseNova's real-robot tests, pick-and-place worked seventeen of eighteen times. Plug insertion: zero for eleven.

beats.narration: The ZAP team at Luma AI says a small open model already understands robot tasks, and mainly lacks motion control.

visual.text: Understands the task. Lacks the motion.

beats.narration: So ZAP teaches that skill entirely in simulation.

beats.narration: The answer: on a real two-armed robot, twenty-nine of thirty trials, matching GPT-6 Astra on the same control software.
